title: The Shocking Truth About Heat Pumps - Energy Vanguard
summary: Energy Vanguard (2013) argues the gas-versus-heat-pump choice depends on climate, rates, fixed charges and the house.

assertions.quote: with rates, efficiencies, and equipment costs all over the map, you can’t make any generalization about always using heat pumps or always using gas heat.
get gas bills in the summer showing no gas consumption and an amount due of $30 or so.
one of their biggest drawbacks: electric resistance heat to supplement the heat pump at low temperatures. Yes, most heat pumps need supplemental heat.
Where cooling loads dominate, heat pumps do, too.
it’s easier and less expensive to get a heat pump small enough to match the loads of a high performance home

verdicts.note: Small inverter heat pumps and mini-splits come in capacities well below the smallest common furnaces.

assertions.quote: find out how many cents per Btu you pay for each fuel, with the equipment efficiency factored in.

verdicts.note: Fuel prices are billed in different units, so a fair comparison converts both to cost per delivered Btu including equipment efficiency.
The comparison converts both fuels to $/MMBtu and divides by AFUE or seasonal COP to get cost per MMBtu of delivered heat.
The evaluators compare systems by the price per delivered Btu, combining each fuel's price, heat content and the appliance's efficiency (COP for the heat pump, AFUE for the furnace).
